Empowering Success Through Holistic and Individualised Learning
ALP Schools are a chain of Independent Special Needs Schools. Each of our schools is Ofsted registered and cater for young people who have struggled in mainstream education due to their special educational needs.
Our unique selling point is that we offer small classes or one to one learning where the curriculum is tailored to the needs of the individual. We also recognise the importance of building routines, relationships, respect and trust in order to achieve successful teaching and learning…

Information for Students, Parents, Teachers and Employees.
We recognise that career advice should start at a young age, therefore, we work in partnership with external careers agencies to ensure all of our learners receive the appropriate information, advice, and guidance concerning their key stage.
Constantly pushing the boundaries to help our young people into employment we work on the ethos of ever-expanding and growing to provide the best service we can offer.
The resources below can help learners and their parents to start thinking about careers. They cover topics such as choosing a career and different routes into the world of work, as well as providing detailed information on specific careers. They can also help students make decisions about the next steps in their education, such as A-level or degree subject choices, and whether or not they’ve decided on a career.

Apprenticeships and Traineeships.
Apprenticeships are officially on the rise. Vacancies for apprentices have risen by 15% over the last year, and applications have increased by almost a third. So, why are so many people in the UK turning to apprenticeships over more traditional career paths? It’s all about the benefits.
Here are five reasons why an apprenticeship could be right for you:
Below are links to national and local sites in relation to finding the right apprenticeship or traineeship for you depending on the school you are based in.

Work Experience.
Employers are very keen on work experience – or rather, they’re keen on what it gives you: the confidence and practical skills you need to succeed in the workplace. Whether or not you’re planning to go to university or college, getting good work experience while you are at school will stand you in good stead when it comes to getting hired.
If you want to apply for an apprenticeship, your work experience will make you a much stronger candidate; if you plan to get a degree, you can draw on it when applying for internships and other placements. It will also give you a better feel for what you do and don’t enjoy and the career choices you want to make.
Gaining work experience arranged through your school is a great start. However, what employers mean by the term can be broader than you might think. All sorts of activities can help to develop the qualities you need at work.
https://targetcareers.co.uk/careers-advice/skills-and-experience/388-work-experience-for-school-students-what-you-need-and-how-to-get-it
Our schools are flexible with our work experience offer. Ideally, every learner will attend one work experience opportunity before year 11 and then complete a second in post 16. This said some of our learners have a consistent day of work experience throughout a school year, others complete their work experience in-house. We are always on the lookout for work experience opportunities, and we appreciate it when parents and students find their own.
All of our work experience opportunities need to be fully risk-assessed before they are approved.
Apprenticeships.
Apprenticeships are another good option for some students. An apprenticeship is a real job where you learn, gain experience, and get paid. You’re an employee with a contract of employment and holiday leave. They also get hands-on training and the chance to put skills into practice. They also get time off work to study for new qualifications or complete ones in English/Maths and ICT. For more information on apprenticeships visit here
Labour Market Information.
Labour Market Information (LMI) is a useful tool to help research future jobs in the local area and understand the skills needed for certain roles and the demand for future employment. It can help predict if the job your child wants will have vacancies/still be needed by the time your child enters the workforce.
What is the ‘Labour Market’?
Labour market information can tell you:
When thinking about your career ideas it is useful to consider what is happening in the labour market; consider what is happening around you and always have ‘back up’ ideas. Here are some useful websites for finding out local Labour Market Information.
National Careers Service
Labour Market Information Kent Districts
Careerometer.
The Careerometer can be used to explore and compare key information about occupations and help you learn about different occupations and identify potential careers. It provides access to a selection of UK headline data relating to pay, weekly hours of work, and future employment prospects for different occupations, as well as a description of the occupation.
Skills Meter.
Case Studies.
There are several routes and pathways into work, University, or employment. Don’t take our word for it. Here are some case studies of learners who had studied with us in the past and have progressed into either work, apprenticeships, or University.
Case Study 1. Learner A came to ALP aged 15 years old after recently being placed into the care of foster parents. Learner A had not been in school for some time and had previously attended a mainstream school. Learner A had a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder. Once settled, learner A accessed a catering program with one of our partner providers and found they had a keen interest in cooking and hospitality. With the support of ALP learner A was successful in securing a place at College on a catering course. Learner A has now completed their course and has gained experience working in the hospitality industry. They currently work full-time in a school kitchen.
Case Study 2. Learner B attended ALP through the school’s outreach program. Learner B suffered from severe agoraphobia and anxiety and due to this was unable to access the school during normal school hours. ALP provided outreach provision in support of gaining the qualifications needed to access further and higher education. One learner B had reached college leaving age, ALP supported them to access further studies that would allow them to gain entry onto an access course at a local university. Learner B is now in their final year of a degree qualification.
Case Study 3. Learner C attended ALP as part of an intervention program through their mainstream school. Learner C was diagnosed with ODD and ADHD and found it very hard to concentrate in a mainstream setting. Learner C eventually came onto the school roll at ALP and found that they enjoyed Construction and working using their hands. Over time ALP was able to support Learner C to access weekly paid work experience with an electrical installation company whilst also attending ALP to ensure they gained numeracy and literacy qualifications to support an application for an apprenticeship.

We are writing to share some positive and exciting news with you. As you will be aware, Parkview Academy has been working hard to improve our provision for parents. We have been working towards an award in Leading Parent Partnership (LPPA). Our auditor visited the school yesterday and was impressed with the progress that we have made with delivering workshops, events and in providing additional support to families. We are very pleased to say that we have secured the award and that we are now a leading school in parent engagement.
We would like to express our appreciation and thanks to everyone who has supported the process and for engaging with our surveys, workshops and events. We will ensure that we maintain our provision for parents and will continue to offer future workshops and events. Please continue to share any comments or feedback that you have as this helps us to continuously improve our provision which, in turn, benefits our students.
Thank you again for your cooperation and support,
Senior Management Team

Make sure you check out below what each individual school achieved this may!
ALP Leicester
To kick off May at ALP Leicester the learners had a fantastic time celebrating the King’s Coronation. It was great to have the whole school together for this special event. (left image)
Then coming into mid May the learners at ALP Leicester participated in 4 different athletic events against other schools. All learners had a fantastic day and came back with a well-deserved medal. (middle image)
After things within May that Leicester were able to discover was the Warning zone. Learners at ALP Leicester and ALP Nuneaton attended the Warning Zone. The Warning Zone is a Leicester-based charity dedicated to teaching life skills and safeguarding children. Learners thoroughly enjoyed the experience (as you can see from the photos).
Coming into the 18th of May, New signage was added to the exterior and the reception area! (below left, below middle photos)Leading into the 22nd of May Learners at ALP have started their level 1 bike ability course by cycletraining@b-buddies.com They enjoyed riding bikes, completing an obstacle course, and learning about the gears and brakes. (below right photo)
ALP Nuneaton
Learners at ALP Leicester and ALP Nuneaton attended the Warning Zone. The Warning Zone is a Leicester-based charity dedicated to teaching life-skills and safeguarding children. Learners thoroughly enjoyed the experience (as you can see from the photos).
Parkview Academy
To kick off May Parkview Academy was extremely excited to share across all socials something one of the learners had been working on! Assassin’s Creed: Unity & Sweet Dreams (We Rabbitz remix cover) AMV: Ollie has created this amateur music video for one of his favorite games. He cut and edited the video and music together in the program Davinci Resolve, making sure that the timing of the two lined up and complemented each other well. This video is part of a series of AMVs he has created for his youtube channel, which he has been using to work towards various AQA awards in his media lessons.
Parkview also had an exciting trip to the Transport Museum in London to have a Geography lesson for their Life Skills students!Next in may the Life Skills students created some amazing artwork to showcase Parkview Academy’s values ARRRTT.
To conclude May before going on half term, Parkview Academy held its second annual Art exhibition! The learners created brilliant artworks, which were sold and all proceeds will go to ‘Ellenor’ charity.
Pierview Academy
For bee week this May, learners at Pierview Academy have been learning about bees, and their importance of them for our planet.
ALP Sittingbourne
ALP Sittingbourne started May by celebrating National Library Week. They updated their school library area and visited the local library to foster our love for reading.
An event that ALP Sittingbourne held in May was a community coronation event. They raised over £900 for the learners to spend on their school environment!

Huge congratulations to the entire ALP Sittingbourne team for attaining a “Good” grading from Ofsted.
This marks a remarkable milestone as all five of our schools have now received the “Good” rating from Ofsted. What a tremendous achievement! A big round of applause to everyone within the ALP Schools community for this outstanding accomplishment.
Here are a few words from our Proprietor (Gemma Gosden) and Head Teacher (Jennifer Thomason) with their comments about the achievement.
“As a group, we have embarked on a lengthy journey to attain these objectives, and we express our profound gratitude to our dedicated staff, valued stakeholders, and collaborative partners for their significant contributions. With the attainment of the “Good” rating across the ALP group, we eagerly anticipate our ongoing commitment to delivering the highest quality education to the children and young individuals under our care.”
“ALP Sittingbourne were visited by Ofsted at the beginning of this term, we were delighted to showcase our wonderful school, staff and students over the three day inspection. It was fantastic to hear our students sharing about their positive experiences including how they “feel they are heard for the first time by the adults that work with them at school”. It was our privilege to share with the inspectors our outdoor learning provision, The Lodge, where our students enjoy animal care, forest school and swimming lessons.
I would like to thank and congratulate my whole staff team who have worked incredibly hard since we opened our doors in September 2022. We are delighted to have achieved a Good grading across the board with Outstanding for Personal Development – the inspectors commented that “Leaders have designed an exceptionally enriching personal development programme that supports each pupil to reengage with education and to understand how school can contribute in a highly positive way to their lives.“

Naagii Lamjav
I joined ASD Learning Ltd in 2013 as it provided me the opportunity of applying my passion of finance to help improve the lives of children and young people with additional learning needs. I could never have imagined however, how our learners would help me improve my own life and continue to be a daily source of inspiration to me so many years later.
naagii.lamjav@alpschools.org

ALP Schools pride ourselves on a quick response to referrals. We will acknowledge your enquiry with a notification to inform you that it has been received. We are likely to then contact you for further information.
If we think that one of our schools may be suitable, we will usually arrange a viewing and meeting with parents and the student.
If our school is at capacity, you will be informed of this and the likely waiting times for a placement.
